thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: SLO breach detected for /v1/generate (p99 > 2.5s) — paging ops-oncall :rotating_light:
ops-oncall: I’m on it, paging triage. Observed big tail around 17:12 UTC, streaming stalls reported by a few customers.
alice: seeing p95 spike from ~120ms -> ~1.4s starting at 17:10. p99 jumps >2s.
ben: same, correlate with increase in auth DB latency. Query times spiking to 800-1200ms for token lookup.
carol: also seeing a rise in `config-fetch` latencies from 30ms -> 900ms. The request path does a per-request config fetch for feature flags.
dmitri: stack traces show requests are waiting on auth DB and then on featureflag service. Could be connection pool exhaustion or a downstream rate-limit.
ops-oncall: quick customer impact check?
support-bot: ~4 customers showing streaming stalls and 5xx errors; overall error rate up from 0.1% -> 1.8%. Most errors are 504/502 on the streaming gateway.
alice: hypothesis: burst of token validation + config fetchs caused DB read replicas to saturate -> auth service times out -> runtime waits and stalls streaming.
ben: I can run a quick `pg_stat_activity` and check slow queries.
carol: also check featureflag service metrics; it has a hard RPS cap per-instance. If it's getting throttled, the control-plane call could block the inference path.
ops-oncall: mitigation plan v1 (quick): 1) enable cached config fallback for requests to avoid per-request roundtrip; 2) bump auth DB read pool and add short-term read replica; 3) increase concurrency knob on featureflag cluster.
ops-oncall: doing step 1 now — flipping fallback flag in console. Command: `kubectl exec -it config-api-5f6 -- curl -XPOST localhost:8080/flags/enable_cache_fallback`
carol: I pushed the flag toggle to `staging` earlier. If you flip it globally we should see config-fetch latencies drop quickly.
alice: starting `pg_stat_activity` check: top queries are `SELECT * FROM tokens WHERE id = $1` with many waiting on `libpq` sockets. Connection pool at 95%.
dmitri: run this to trace auth service latency: `curl -sS http://auth-service.internal/metrics | grep request_duration`
ops-oncall: ran the curl, auth p95 went from 40ms -> 1.1s. We have a backlog of auth validation calls.
ben: temporary mitigation: apply rolling restart of auth pods to clear stuck connections and ramp up replicas. Command: `kubectl scale deployment auth --replicas=6` then monitor.
elaine: I can run the scale and monitor logs, taking the second half of this incident. Handoff at 17:30 UTC.
ops-oncall: doing replica scale now. Also enabling short circuit that uses token cache TTL=30s for repeated requests from same token to reduce load.
carol: featureflag team: we can add a local cache layer to the SDK so a missed FF lookup doesn't block the request. Adding 500ms fallback timeout to the fetch.
dmitri: pushing a temporary rate-limit increase for internal control-plane service account used by runtime: `POST /admin/ratelimits/service_account/runtime_controlplane/increase?by=2x`
support-bot: customer note drafted: "We observed elevated latency and streaming stalls from ~17:10-17:45 UTC. Root cause under investigation. Some customers experienced increased tail latency and transient 5xx responses. We're applying mitigations now."
ops-oncall: after toggles and scale, p95 down to ~220ms, p99 ~560ms. Streaming error rate back to ~0.35%.
alice: good improvement. Need to confirm there's no data corruption. All checks show token DB reads consistent.
dmitri: logs show a burst of retries from a third-party integration hitting the token service — looks like a misbehaving client created the burst.
ben: we'll add a soft quota and per-client cooldown to avoid single-client amplifying the control-plane. Also limit accept queue length on auth service.
elaine: taking over incident lead. Summary for handoff: root cause - control-plane dependency saturation (auth DB + featureflag fetch) amplified by a client burst and per-request config fetch; mitigations applied - cache fallback, scaled auth replicas, increased FF timeouts, rate-limit tweak, rolling restarts; current state - latency improving, monitoring in progress.
ops-oncall: handing off to elaine. My pager clear.
elaine: thanks — I'll follow up with customers and start a postmortem draft. Immediate action items: 1) permanent token cache or short-lived cache in runtime; 2) SDK local FF cache + fail-open; 3) add per-client soft quotas and throttling; 4) improve observability for control-plane tails (traces linking runtime->auth->ff).
carol: agree. I'll open PRs for SDK changes and config fallback metrics.
alice: I'll own DB connection pool tuning + adding a read-replica automation runbook.
dmitri: I'll prepare a remediation playbook for future bursts and a dashboard with per-client QPS distribution.
ops-oncall: incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations applied, oncall handed off to elaine. We'll publish incident summary after postmortem. :white_check_mark:
elaine: tagging product + support for customer comms: @product @support — will coordinate message.
support-bot: queued customer updates for affected orgs, scheduled follow-up once postmortem is available.
incident-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED (mitigated) — create postmortem in #postmortems and link here.
elaine: creating postmortem draft now. Will include timeline, root cause, mitigations, and action owners.
